headline: Enes Kanter Freedom Sues Chicago Sky: Odds of Man Being Drafted to WNBA Down to 4%

body.text: At one point, when Enes Kanter Freedom first declared for the WNBA, his odds of being drafted were as high as 31%. That was back when Polymarket had a market specifically for Freedom to be drafted. Now, the site is only offering bets on "any former NBA player to be drafted," and the price has slipped all the way to 4%.

body.caption: Polymarket odds: any former NBA player is drafted in the 2027 WNBA Draft

body.text: In the latest dramatic event in the tale, which already seems like complete fantasy, Freedom is suing Chicago Sky. He was kicked out of a game by the team's security staff last month when he found himself in a verbal altercation with Natasha Cloud. The lawsuit also names the City of Chicago and Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority.

Freedom has declared himself eligible for the WNBA draft in an attempt to protest trans participation in the league, claiming that there is nothing stopping him from declaring himself a woman and playing in the league. At the Chicago Sky game, he was illustrating his point with a tshirt that said the definition of a woman is an "adult human female."
My T-shirt did what the whole WNBA apparently couldn't: define a woman

The former NBA pro took to X on Thursday this week to claim that he has filed a federal complaint against Chicago Sky. "I'm taking legal action over my ejection," Freedom wrote, arguing that he was kicked out while exercising his "First Amendment rights." He said: "My T-shirt did what the whole WNBA apparently couldn't: define a woman."

Freedom isn't alone in his stunt. Royce White, another former NBA pro, has also declared himself eligible for the draft. Last month, he showed up at an Indiana Fever game sporting a blonde wig. He claimed he was there to "scout some of the competition" and support the league.

According to the [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/wnba-enes-kanter-freedom-royce-white-4b23db1f7817caa2a5de018fa7c94b86), a source close to the matter has claimed that Freedom and White are not eligible for the league. The anonymous source did not, however, explain why they were ineligible.

The topic shot into the headlines again this week after false reports began circling that trans basketball player Julie Tetart had declared for the draft. In fact, the French player told outlet Outkick that she would not refuse the opportunity to play if a WNBA team got in touch, but said nothing about declaring for the draft.

author: Owain Flanders
